correctness.rationale: For nonempty finite k-multitournaments in the pure k-tournament language, the two-round Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé game is exactly determined by the set of local outgoing q=2^k orientation-signature sets. The q+1 lower bound is degree; a cyclic odd-order K_(q+1) two-factorization labels each incident arc by one of all q complementary signatures. Conditioning on the single shared oriented edge leaves disjoint edge collections at two vertices, and color symmetry makes each deficiency conditional rate independent of the shared signature; the exact variance follows. For n/q=2 log q+log log q+c+o(1), missing-coupon Bonferroni gives p~q(1-1/q)^(n-1) and factorial moments of the marked deficient vertices converge to (2e^-c)^r after conditioning on finitely many internal edges, establishing Poisson(2e^-c), not merely a variance heuristic. No fixed-language window is claimed.
